newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt up as focus on Russian eurobond continues.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt up as focus on Russian eurobond continues.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly higher at late afternoon as continued optimism over the upcoming Russian Eurobond helped to push the country's debt instruments slightly higher, traders said.

"The roadshow on the Russian Eurobond has gone very well," said one emerging market debt trader at a major U.S. investment bank, who expects the yield spreads on Russian loans to continue to narrow in coming weeks.
At 1615 EST/2115 GMT, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were 1/4 firmer at 80-3/4 bid and its Min Fin 3s were one percentage point higher at 83 bid.
However, another source from a major U.S. bank said that he did not see much more upside for the Russian loans.

"Quite frankly, I think the tightening we have seen in Russia has pretty much priced in whatever good news comes out of a new Eurobond," the second source said. "I think we will have to have something new other than the consummation of the Eurobond to drive it significantly higher."
The roadshow for the Russian Eurobond began last week in Europe and is expected to make its way to New York on Tuesday.
According to market sources, the size of the deal is expected to be about $500 million and could be priced as tight as 300 basis points over U.S. Treasury securities.
Bulgaria was another favorite of the day as expectations of a currency board helped to boost its prices. The country's IABs were 3/8 higher at 48-1/2 bid and its FLRBs were 1/8 firmer at 35-3/4 bid.
"Bulgaria is up strongly. It continues to be fairly well bid on the back of what people think will be a currency board," a trader said.
Among the Latin American Brady bonds, Brazilian loans posted the biggest gains, which traders attributed mostly to shortcovering by local players. Brazil's "C" bonds were up 7/8 at 72 bid.

Meanwhile, a better-than-expected report on Mexico's September industrial output helped lend support to its Brady debt. Mexico Finance Ministry said Monday that its industrial activity grew 14 percent in September compared with the same month last year.
Mexico's par bonds were 1/8 better at 72-1/2 bid and its UMS-26 were 1/8 firmer at 103-1/8 bid.
Elsewhere, Argentine FRBs were 1/4 stonger at 85 bid and Venezuela's DCBs were 1/4 higher at 84-5/8 bid.
